title: BDD slice A: three café scenarios, with a real-agent measurement
item: Build the BDD tests for café scenarios SC-08, SC-12 and SC-10 end to end, prove them on a scripted agent, and measure with a throwaway real LLM agent whether their verdicts are right
motivation: First slice of task 1. It tests the riskiest assumption before anything larger is built: that tests proven on a scripted agent give right verdicts on a real LLM agent. It also shows the test format to the owner on 3 scenarios.
notes: The full description is the section 'Slice A' of tasks/plans/001.md; read the whole plan first, terms included. Work goes in .claude/skills/agent-spec-to-pytest-bdd/examples/cafe/ (no SKILL.md yet; the skill is written in a later slice). The spec is .claude/skills/agent-spec/examples/cafe/spec/; read it, and read .claude/skills/agent-spec/scripts/check.py for how a scenario replays through model.py; edit neither. Build in the plan's order, data file first. Save every probe-agent transcript in one folder and the checkers' verdicts in another, so the transcripts can be labelled without seeing the verdicts. Part 2 calls the Claude API. The owner is logged in with the ant CLI (`ant auth login`) and has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set; do not park for a missing key. Run `ant auth status` first. Use, in this order: the Python SDK if it picks up the ant login by itself; else the SDK with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN set from `ant auth print-credentials --access-token`, fetched again when a call is refused as expired; else `ant messages create` as a subprocess. Never write a token or key to a file or a log. Only if `ant auth status` shows no login and no key is set: finish part 1, write that under needs_you and park. Spend at most 5 USD on part 2 and report what was spent. The probe agent's model is a draft choice: a mid-size current Claude model, named in the report. Do not open the branch add-agent-spec-to-pytest-bdd. RETRY, 2026-11-17. Part 1 was built on branch task/049 and passed its second review (tasks/reviews/049-2.md): carry that work over, do not rebuild it. The owner has accepted the feature-file format and has added API credit; if a call is refused as expired, the owner must run `ant auth login` again, so park with that as the one question. Before running part 2, fix what task 054 listed (folded into this task): the fake has only 3 hold ids and 3 confirmation ids, so a 4th hold or booking raises IndexError and stops later runs; a run that raises after API calls loses its usage from money spent; data.json names tests/test_harness.py where the file is tests/test_part1.py; a transcript shows the confirmation id of an unanswered booking call, which the agent must not see. Also add the data-file checks now in line 3 of done_means, as script tests. After part 2 has run: do not label the transcripts yourself. Provide a script that reads a labels file (one pass or fail per run and rule, written later by Claude in chat) and prints line 4's agreement count, every disagreement, and line 5; then park with the question 'bring runs/part2/transcripts/ to chat for labelling', leaving runs/part2/verdicts/ in a separate folder.
done_means: For SC-08, SC-12 and SC-10: (1) 3 of 3 pass with the reference agent, with 0 LLM calls; (2) each of the 2 broken variants (R-03, R-11) fails the Then sentence of its own rule; (3) every value a step, the fake or a replayed history uses comes from the data file; every entry there is labelled 'from the spec' or 'free choice'; script tests show that each 'from the spec' entry cites a claim or rule id that exists in the spec, that its number or quoted words appear in the cited text (an entry whose wording is the builder's own says so), and that each value fits its scenario label (the value for '8 or fewer' is at most 8); the drift check covers the data file as well as the feature files, and the feature files equal the script's output; (4) on the 27 one-action probe runs the rule checkers agree with the labels Claude in chat gives the transcripts on at least 9 of every 10 rule verdicts, every disagreement listed; (5) for each of the 2 bad prompts at least 1 run shows the bad behaviour and is failed on its rule. Reported with the result: runs that reach a verdict out of 27 and out of 9 whole conversations, pass rate per rule, money spent.

Lines 1 to 3 of done_means are for script and reviewer; lines 4 and 5 need the owner to bring the transcripts to chat, which is why verified_by includes you. decided_for_you.chosen: Probe model claude-sonnet-5-5, priced at grading.json model_rates.sonnet ($2 in / $10 out per million)
decided_for_you.rejected: Another model, or prices from elsewhere
decided_for_you.would_change: If you name another model or the real sonnet-5-5 price differs

decided_for_you.chosen: Each tested moment runs in one home scenario and is judged on that scenario's cited rules
decided_for_you.rejected: Judging every scenario's rules at every moment, which adds trivially held verdicts and inflates line 4's agreement
decided_for_you.would_change: If you want the union of rules; change moments.*.scenario and CITED
